body.en: A *differential amplifier* has two inputs and amplifies their difference. With inputs $V_1$ and $V_2$, the difference signal is $V_d = V_1 - V_2$ and the common-mode signal is $V_c = (V_1 + V_2)/2$. The output is $V_o = A_dV_d + A_cV_c$, where $A_d$ is the differential gain and $A_c$ the (small) common-mode gain. The common-mode rejection ratio $\text{CMRR} = A_d/A_c$, often in dB, measures how well signals common to both inputs, such as hum and noise, are rejected. Ideally $A_c = 0$ and CMRR is infinite.

narration.en: A differential amplifier amplifies the difference of its two inputs and rejects what is common to both. CMRR is the ratio of differential to common-mode gain.
narration.kn: ಡಿಫರೆನ್ಷಿಯಲ್ ವರ್ಧಕ ಎರಡು ಇನ್‌ಪುಟ್‌ಗಳ ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸವನ್ನು ವರ್ಧಿಸಿ ಸಾಮಾನ್ಯ ಭಾಗವನ್ನು ತಿರಸ್ಕರಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. CMRR = Ad/Ac.

body.en: An operational amplifier is a very high gain, direct-coupled *differential amplifier*. Its block diagram has a differential input stage (high input resistance and CMRR), an intermediate gain stage, a level shifter that brings the DC level back to zero, and a push-pull output stage (low output resistance). Being direct-coupled, it amplifies DC as well as AC. In the 8-pin IC 741: pin 2 inverting input, pin 3 non-inverting input, pin 6 output, pin 7 +VCC, pin 4 −VEE, pins 1 and 5 offset null, pin 8 no connection.

myth.en: In a non-inverting amplifier the gain is R_f / R₁, the same as an inverting one but positive.

truth.en: Non-inverting gain is 1 + R_f / R₁. It is never less than 1. The '1' comes from the divider: the − input sees only the fraction R₁/(R₁ + R_f) of the output. Forgetting it is the most common slip in this chapter.

say.en: Two ideal assumptions drive every derivation: V₊ = V₋ and zero input current.
Non-inverting gain = 1 + R_f/R₁; inverting gain = −R_f/R₁.

steps.en: The common-mode part (2 mV) is an error of 20%: this CMRR is poor.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. A differential amplifier has Ad = 1000 and Ac = 10. The inputs are V1 = 205 µV and V2 = 195 µV. Find Vo and the CMRR in dB.

say.en: Let us work this out together. A differential amplifier has Ad equals 1000 and Ac equals 10. The inputs are V1 equals 205 µV and V2 equals 195 µV. Find Vo and the CMRR in dB.
Vd equals 205 minus 195 equals 10 µV; Vc equals 205 plus 195/2 equals 200 µV.
Vo equals 1000 times 10 µV plus 10 times 200 µV equals 10 mV plus 2 mV equals 12 mV.
CMRR equals 1000 over 10 equals 100 equals 20 log 100 equals 40 dB.
The common-mode part 2 mV is an error of 20 percent: this CMRR is poor.
So the answer is Vo equals 12 mV; CMRR equals 40 dB.
